public_rationale: Reporting documents Copilot interface intrusions and uneven disabling options. It does not establish that most Word and Excel users hated Copilot. A government trial found positive sentiment, but its earlier, restricted sample cannot settle the broader June 2025 claim.
limitations: Neither complaints nor a selected workplace trial establish sentiment among all affected users.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Microsoft bloats Word and Excel with odd interface choices and makes users fight with popups to use an AI-powered Copilot that most of them hate.

statement.excerpt: Products like Word and Excel don’t need improving, but that doesn’t stop Microsoft from trying, bloating them with odd user interface choices and forcing users to fight with popups to use an AI-powered Copilot that most of them hate.

from_speaker: forcing users to fight with popups
Copilot that most of them hate
our_interpretation: The checkable components are intrusive Copilot prompts and majority dislike among affected Word and Excel users.
Most means more than half. Hate is read as strong dislike, not merely non-use or dissatisfaction with one feature.
The ongoing state is assessed for June 2025, the current month at publication. This period is an evaluator choice because the speaker supplies none.
Odd interface choices and bloat are subjective descriptions, not separate numerical tests.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous interface records establish intrusive prompts in Word and Excel, and a representative survey establishes that more than half of affected users strongly dislike Copilot.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable interface records disprove the claimed prompting behavior, or a representative survey establishes that no majority of the relevant users strongly dislikes Copilot.

evidence.explanation: The article describes per-app disabling options for some subscriptions and their absence for others. This limits any reading that every user faced the same unavoidable interface.
This government trial found substantial positive sentiment. Its September–December 2024 participants and suite-wide questions do not represent all Word and Excel users in June 2025.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A representative survey of the relevant June 2025 users, with direct sentiment questions, alongside dated interface records covering the affected versions.
